direction: Still of the place John describes. A hawthorn hedge tops the railway embankment below the hill at Llandough. Apple trees heavy with August fruit lean over it, and the iron rails run below toward Penarth. A thin drift of lime-kiln smoke rises from the far hillside. No people and no train. Slow push along the hedge line. Ambience: wasps, wind in leaves, a distant train whistle. About 20 seconds.

captions.text: 15 Dec 1887: Daniel Thomas of Penylan dies. He was a contractor under Lord Bute, with lime kilns at Llandough.
24 Apr 1888: A man is described as a labourer at Llandough Quarry.
